title: Cap. IX Arg.: Major confirmed — Adam received; Christ obtained reconciliation for all; therefore reprobation only from final impenitence
pass_a_gloss: They try to confirm the Major twofold. First, from this, that pardon was given to Adam himself: For it would seem iniquitous that God on account of the sin of Adam, which by pure mere estimation of his is ours, should exclude any others whatsoever from eternal life, when he received into grace Adam himself, who perpetrated that sin. Secondly, they strive to prove the same from this, that Christ obtained redemption and reconciliation with God the Father for all; but it seems little agreeable that by the decree of reprobation they be left unto destruction, for whom Christ so obtained reconciliation that nothing can impede, besides impenitence, whereby they may become partakers of the use of the same. Therefore no one is reprobated except from consideration of final impenitence or rebellion as moving cause: but this is reprobation.
pass_b_english: They try to confirm the Major two ways. First: pardon was given to Adam himself — so it would seem unjust that God, for Adam's sin which by mere estimation is called ours, should shut any others from eternal life, when he received into grace Adam who committed that sin. Second: Christ obtained redemption and reconciliation with the Father for all — and it seems little fitting that by a reprobation decree those be left to destruction for whom Christ so obtained reconciliation that nothing but impenitence can bar them from sharing its use. Therefore no one is reprobated except from regard to final impenitence or rebellion as moving cause — and that, they say, is reprobation.
source_text: Majorem dupliciter confirmare conantur. Primo, exinde quod ipsi Adamo venia data sit: Iniquum enim videatur Deum ob Adami peccatum, quod pura puta illius aestimatione nostrum est, alios quoscunque a vita aeterna excludere, cum ipsum Adamum receperit in gratiam, qui illud peccatum perpetravit. Secundo, idem probare satagunt ex eo quod Christus pro omnibus redemptionem et reconciliationem apud Deum Patrem impetravit; videtur autem parum consentaneum, ut per decretum reprobationis exitio relinquantur, pro quibus Christus ita reconciliationem impetravit, ut nihil impedire possit, praeter impoenitentiam, quo minus ejusdem usu fiant participes. Ergo nemo reprobatur nisi ex consideratione finalis impoenitentiae sive rebellionis tanquam causae motivae: haec autem reprobatio.
